main_text.head: Cap. 5. De notatione.
main_text.p: Derivata sæpe quantitatem mutant, præsertim cùm alteram vocalem tollunt, ut á πείθω suadeo, prima brevi πειθὼς suasibilis: item á φεύγω fugio, φυγὴ fuga: μανία furor primam corripit, μανικὸς furiosus producit. Commutat verò etiam compositio accentum, ut σοφὸς sapiens, φιλόσοφος philosophus: αὐτὸς ipse, φίλαυτος amâs sui: quod in monosyllabis perpetuum est, ut πᾶς puer, ἀγαθὸς bonus-puer (vel felix liberis): γῆν terra, αὐτόχθων indigena: πούς pes, πολύπους multipes. Properispomena accentu retrahunt in præcedentem, ut δῆλος servus δι-δῆλος benignus servis: μοῦσα inusa, ἐμ-μουσος in quo musica concinnitas inest.

page.notes: Greek words are transcribed as legible; some accents are uncertain in the scan (the running head and the Greek forms in the middle of the page are partly faded). The word "inusa" and "ἐμ-μουσος" are doubtful; the sentence fragment at the end is a catchword broken at the line end. The printed "iiij" signature reads "iiij" in the scan.
